body: Looks like this is a problem with the plain text version of the HTML mail that is generated automatically and thus contains HTML encoded parts. Can you paste the source text of the email? You may grep the .eml file from the debug toolbar for this.

Here is the content of the .eml file:

https://gist.github.com/evercode1/fc8fa6ce87dd39a45818

It looks like it is broken in both the plain text and html version.
Can you show the content of `passwordResetToken.php`?

Sorry, I don't see a file by that name.  I do have requestPasswordResetToken.php in frontend/views/site:

https://gist.github.com/evercode1/2d86680f26c69d2af10e

This is from a fresh install today, not modified in any way.  Please let me know if I need to look for a different file.
It's `common/mail/passwordResetToken.php`. This is the template file for generating the mail.

this what I have for passwordResetToken.php:

https://gist.github.com/evercode1/d6658b64423808cf85ff
Seems it's caused by MIME encoding which is expected to encode `=` into `%3D`. But in your pasted eml, they are encoded as `=3D`.
When I changed the url manually in the browser, the rest of the process worked perfectly, so I think the encoding issue is the only issue.

The problem is that we only specify a HTML layout and template and yii generates a text from that: https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/framework/mail/BaseMailer.php#L203
Thus the Html encoded link will appear in a plain text email and will of course not work there:
https://github.com/yiisoft/yii2/blob/master/apps/advanced/common/mail/passwordResetToken.php#L14

We could check if we can enhance the html->text converter or provide a text only template or both.
Small email providers may not support html email correctly, so it's probably vital to have a text version at minimum.
A bit strange: `Html::encode($resetLink)` shouldn't cause the problem described in this issue when it is converted into text.

@evercode1 we always have the text fallback the problem is that it is broken ;)
@qiangxue why not? if you encode an URL that contains `&` you will have `&` instead and the URL is invalid when represented as plain text.
True, but the problem reported here is about `=3D`, which is strange.

This is the encoded URL:

```
http://yiifresh.com/index.php?r=3Dsite%2Freset-password&token=
=3Db4n2OQmr4mdhrDrGiqQs-i5u09_dpxmX_1420392550
```

It is encoded 2 times:
1. Html::encode()
2. MIME quoted-printable

decoding the MIME will give us:

```
http://yiifresh.com/index.php?r=site%2Freset-password&token=b4n2OQmr4mdhrDrGiqQs-i5u09_dpxmX_1420392550
```

What is left is the HTML encoding which we now need to revert too.
I see. I think we should provide a text version then.
